lawyer:
Moudud Ahmed and Samiran Das Gopta and Mohammad Motaher Hossain, Advocates--For the Petitioner. 
Syed Shahidur Rahman and Md Jahangir Advocates--For the Opposite Party No.1.
parties:
Harun-ur Rashid (Md) ------ Pre-emptee-Petitioner
vs
Rashed Harun and others ------ Pre-emptee-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 13-2-2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in Misc. (Pre-emption) Appeal No. 56 of 2010 allowing the appeal and setting-aside the judgment and order dated 24-2-2010 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Patiya, Chittagong in Pre-emption Misc. Case No. 76 of 2005 disallowing the pre-emption should not be set aside

2. Relevant facts, in short, are that the opposite party No.1 as pre-emptor filed Pre-emption Case No.76 of 2005 in the Court of the Senior Assistant  Judge, 1st Court, Patiya, Chittagong for pre-empting the case land as described in the schedule of the application.

3. The case of the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1, in-short, is that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 is a co-sharer to the case jote.

4. The vendor-opposite party No. 2, Kanchan Miah alias Motahar Mean without serving any notice upon him transferred the case land to the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1 (present petitioner), who is stranger to the case jote. Hence, the case.

5. The pre-emptee-petitioner resisted the pre-emption application by filing written statement denying most of the allegations of the pre-emption application contending, inter-alia; that the case land originally belonged to Simad Miah, Thanda Miah, Sydur Haque and others; Samad Miah and Thanda Minh transferred their share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 14-6-1940 and Sydul Haque also transferred his share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 2-6-1934 and after the death of Ezahar Meah his son Kanchan Miah alias Motahar Mean inherited the entire land and accordingly, his name finally published in BS Khatian. Thereafter, Kanchan Miah transferred the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner on 6-7-2005 by registered deed with the full knowledge of the pre-emptor and other co-sharers and after purchasing the property the pre-emptee-purchaser mutated his name by opening mutation Khatian No. 2645. The pre-emptee purchaser has many lands surrounding the case land and that he is not a stranger to the case land. It has been also stated that the pre-emptor-opposite party is not a co-sharer at all and, as such, the case is liable to be dismissed.

6. At the trial pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 (present opposite party No. 1) examined in all 3 PWs and the pre-emptee purchaser (present petitioner) examined in all 2 OPWs and also exhibited the documents to prove their respective cases.

7. The trial Court after closing of the evidence and hearing argument of both the parties by his judgment and order dated 24-2-2010 dis-allowed the pre-emption on the ground that the pre-emptor could not prove that he is a co-sharer to the case jote.

8. The unsuccessful pre-emptor, there-upon, preferred Misc. Appeal No.56 of 2010 before the teamed District Judge, Chittagong, which was eventually heard and disposed of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong, who by the impugned judgment and order dated 13-2-2013 allowed the appeal and set-aside the judgment passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, In Court, Patiya, Chittagong on the finding that in the facts and circumstance of the case the trial Court below commix ted illegality in holding that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case jote and the instant Revision application is directed against that judgment.

9. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptee-petitioner after placing the impugned order as well as the judgment of the Mal Court below submits that the impugned order is not at all a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch the Court of appeal below without adverting the findings of the trial Court below abruptly arrived at a finding that the trial Court below committed illegality in holding that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case jote. Mr Moudud Ahmed further upon referring the evidence of OPWs submits that the pre-emptee purchaser himself was examined as OPW-1, who in his evidence categorically stated that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case land and the pre-emptee purchaser is a co-sharer to the case jote and he has more land surrounding the case land but the Court of appeal below as last Court of fact without considering the evidence of OPWs and without adverting the material finding of the trial Court below most illegally set-aside the judgment of the trial Court below which resulted in the failure of justice. Finally, Mr Moudud Ahmed submits that as per mutation Khatian No.2962 the co-sharer ship of the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 has been ceased and since the pre-emptor lost his co-sharer ship by separating his joma through Mutation Case No.7396 of 2011 he cannot apply for pre-emption. 10. Drawing support of his submission, the learned Advocate has relied on a decision reported in 55 DLR 214.

11. Mr Syed Shahidur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and order which was according to him just, correct and proper. Mr Shahidur Rahman in the course of his argument upon placing judgments of two Courts below, deposition of witnesses submits that the pre-emptor in his deposition as well as pre-emption application categorically stated that he become a co-sharer to the case land by inheritance and thus, the Court of appeal below committed no illegality in holding that the trial Court com-mitted wrong in arriving at a finding that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case land. The learned Advocate further submits that PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 categorically stated in their respective testimony that the pre-emptor-purchaser is stranger to the case jote and the claim of the pre-emptee-opposite party that he is a co- sharer to the case jote is false and without any legal basis. Finally, Mr Shahid Rahman, relied on the decisions reported in 35 DLR (AD) 54 and 34 DLR 180, and submits that the findings of the Court of appeal below are well founded in law and facts that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. I is a co-sharer to the case jote and he is entitled to pre-empt the land, is well founded in law and fact and the same should not be disturbed.

12. Heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the revision application, deposition of witnesses, judgments of two Courts below and other materials on record.

13. The main point for consideration is as already noticed whether the Court of appeal below was justified in holding that the trial Court below committed wrong in arriving at a finding that the pre-emptor could not prove that he is a co-sharer to the case jote.

14. It appears that in this case pre-emptor himself was examined as PW-1, who in his cross-examination stated that:- বি, এস, ২১৩৩ ও ২১৩৯ নং খতিয়ানে আমার নাম নাই। বি এস, রেকর্ডীয় মুস্তাফিজুর রহমান মারা যায় । তাদের ওযারিশ কয়জন জানিনা। কাঞ্চন মিয়াকে পক্ষ করেছি। বি এস, রেকডীয় মরিয়ম খাতুনকে চিনি না। নালিশী ভূমি বি, এস, ২১৩৩ ও ২১৩৯ খতিয়ানের ভূমি। ১নং প্রতিপক্ষের দাখিলী । জবাব পড়ি নাই। ১নং প্রতিপক্ষের নামে নালিশী জমি সম্পর্কে বি এস, ৬৪৫ নং নামজারি খতিয়ান হয়েছে কিনা জানিনা।

15. Pre-emptee-purchaser himself was examined as OPW-1, who in his deposition stated that:- নালিশী ভূমির চর্তুদিকে আমার জমি । ঐ ভূমি ২৩-১১-২০০২ ইং তারিখের ৭০২২ নং কবলা মুলে খরিদ করি।This witness also stated that:- নামজারী খতিয়া্ন মূলে জমা ভাগ করেছি। প্রার্থীকে আমার হোল্ডিং এ শরীক নহে।

16. OPW-2, Md Ali stated in his deposition that:- আমি প্রাথির্ক ১নং প্রতিপক্ষকে চিনি । নারিশী ভুমির আশে পাশে সকল জমি ১নং প্রতিপক্ষের। নাঃ জমি ১নং প্রতিপক্ষের জন্য আবশীকীয়।

17. It appears from the "Exhibit No. Kha" that the pre-emptee-purchaser after purchasing the case land mutated his name.

18. From the above quoted evidence, it appears that both the parties are claiming that they are co-sharer to the case jote.

19. On going through the pre-emption application and written objection, it appears that the case land originally belonged to Samad Miah, Thanda Miah, Sydur Haque and others; Samad Miah and Thanda Miah transferred their share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 14-6-1940 and Sydul Haque also transferred his share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 2-6-1934 and after the death of Ezahar Meah his son Kanchan Miah alias Motahar Meah inherited the entire land and accordingly, his name finally published in B.S. Khatian, who sold out the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner on 6-7-2005 by registered deeds and father of the pre-emptor named Alhaj Mvi. Md Harun Islamabadi purchased the land from the brother of Motahar (brother of Kanchan Miah) from the case holding by registered deeds dated 9-10-1997, 19-6-1997, 21-1-1998, 5-8-1997 and 13-4-1997 and in this way the father of the pre-emptor became co-sharer to the case holding in the year 1997 and the pre-emptee purchaser became co-sharer to the case holding in the year 2005. It further appears that both the parties after purchasing the land from parent joma mutated their names.

20. On considering all these aspects of the case together with the findings of the trial Court below, I do not find any reason that pre-emptor purchaser is a stranger to the case jote and the pre-emptor opposite party is a co-sharer to the case jote and he is entitled to preempt the case land.

21. In this connection, I must quote a pas-sage from the judgment of the trial Court, which reads as follows:

“পযালোচনায় দেখা যায় প্রার্থীর অগ্রক্রয় আবেদনে তার পূরর্বর্তী মাওলানা হারুন ইসলামামাদী আর এস, রেকডীয় স্বত্ববান ব্যক্তিগণ হতে না তাদের ওয়ারিশ হতে খরিদ পূবর্ক স্বত্ববান ও দখলকার ছিলেন তা সুস্পষ্টভাবে উল্লেখ করেননি। আর এস রেকর্ডীয় স্বত্ববান ব্যক্তিগণ কোন কোন ব্যক্তিকে স্বত্ববান ওয়ারিশ রেখে মৃত্যুবরণ করেন। উক্ত বিষয়ে ও সুস্পষ্ট বর্ণনা প্রার্থীর অগ্রক্রয় আবেদনে উল্লেখ নাই। নালিশী আশিয়া মৌজাসহ অত্র এলাকায় হাল বি এস, জরীপে বি, এস,খতিয়ান ���ুড়ান্ত ভাবে প্রচারিত হয়ে পৃথক জোত জমার সৃষ্টি হয়েছে। আইনের বিধান মতে অগ্রক্রয় আবেদন হাল জোত জমার উপর নির্ভরশীল । নালীশী মোজায় নালিশী আর এস ১৪৪৩ আর এস ১৪২০ এবং আর এস ১৪৯০ নং থতিয়ানের ভূমি বাবদ কত নম্বর হাল বি, এস, খতিয়ান চুড়ান্ত ভাবে প্রস্তুত ও প্রচারিত হয়েছে তা প্রার্থীর আবেদনে উল্লেখ করা হয় নি। হাল বি, এস, জরীপে কোন কোন ব্যক্তি শরীক প্রজা এবং প্রার্থীর অগ্রক্রয় আবেদনে সুস্পষ্ট ভাবে উল্লেখ নাই।প্রার্থী কতিপয় দলিল দাখিল করে নালিশী জোতের ভূমিতে শরীফ প্রজা দাবী করলেও তার অগ্রক্রয় আবেদর হাল জোত জমা এবং উক্তজোত জমার শরীকান সম্পর্কে উপযুক্ত বর্ণনা সংযোজন না করায় প্রার্থী নালিশী কবলার ভূমিতে শরীক প্রজা দাতার বিষয়ে স্পষ্ট ও খরচ ধাবনা পাওয়া গেল না। প্রার্থীর অগ্রক্রয় আবেদনের বক্তব্য অস্পষ্ট এবং দ্বার্থক মর্মে সাব্যস্ত হল।”

22. This being a purely a finding of fact based on assessment of the evidence on record that the pre-emptor could not establish a clear case that he is a co-sharer to the case jote. Therefore, in the facts and circumstance of the case, I am led to hold that the court of appeal below committed illegality in rejecting the finding of the trial Court on the point that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer.

23. Another bane of contention raised in this revision that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal.

24. On a reading of the impugned judgment together with the judgment of the trial Court, it appears that the Judge of the appellate court without adverting the proper material finding of the trial Court below arrived at a finding that:-বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতে প্রার্থীর শরিকদার না হওয়া সম্পর্কে যে সমস্ত বিষয়ে বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ক্রটি বিচ্যুতির তথ্য উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন তাহা গ্রহনযোগ্য নহে । নিম্ন আদলতে দায়েরকৃত আরজী জবাবের এই সমস্ত ভুল ক্রুটি মামলার গভীরে প্রবেশ করিলে উপেক্ষিত হইতে পারে।

25. This finding of the trial Court indicates that the Court of appeal below without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstance of the case mechanically set-aside the judgment of the trial Court below.

26. Further at the trial thereupon, referring Ext. B and mutation case No. 7396 of 2011 Mr Moudud Ahmed argues that the pre-emptor losses his co-sharer ship in the tenancy or holding by separating his joma through a mutation and thus, he cannot get his right of pre-emption this important question was not raised before the Courts below.

27. On perusal of the record, I find nothing on the record to suggest that important question was raised before the Courts below by any of the parties.

<u>28. On a perusal of the Ext. B and mutation being Mutation Case No.7396 of 2011, it appears that both the parties separated their joma by mutating their names in respect of the case land and, as such, I find good deal of substance in the contention raised by Mr Moudud Ahmed that the pre-emptor lost his right for pre-emption and accepted the same.</u>

29. Here, it may further be mentioned that the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite party No.1 have no manner of application as the facts of the present case are quite distinguishable from the facts of those cases.

30. For the reasons stated above, I am inclined to hold that the learned Joint District Judge without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstance of the case and law bearing on the subject most illegally set-aside the judgment of the trial Court below, which resulted in the failure of justice.

31. The Rule is, therefore, made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 13-2-2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 250 Court, Chittagong in Misc. (Pre-emption) Appeal No. 56 of 2010 is set-aside. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Courts record be sent down at once.

End.
